description: Issue #1024 (Phase 1, reduced): the adjudication for the FileAttachment.Path storage-identity attack (the tenant filter protects the FileAttachments metadata row, not the blob its Path points at) established that the attack needs a writer that can set FileAttachment PERSISTED FIELDS -- precondition (a) -- and that (a) does not hold in the current tree. The 'why' had zero test coverage: it rests entirely on BaseCRUDVM.DoAddPrepareCore's de-duplication loop (own comment: '将所有TopBasePoco的属性赋空值，防止添加关联的重复内容' -- 'null every TopBasePoco property to prevent duplicate related content on add'), which nulls every TModel-declared property whose type is/derives from TopBasePoco -- including a scalar FileAttachment-typed navigation property -- BEFORE DoAddPrepare's terminal `DC.Set<TModel>().Add(Entity)` call. That call is a real DbSet<T>.Add(), which performs EF Core's full recursive graph-tracking walk (TrackGraph), discovering and marking Added every reachable object. Without the nulling, a caller posting a nested `Photo: { ID, Path, FileName, ... }` object on ANY model with a scalar FileAttachment nav property (e.g. this repo's own Student.Photo) would have that nested object cascade-Added and its attacker-chosen Path INSERTed straight into the FileAttachments table -- with zero involvement of WtmFileProvider, the upload endpoint, or any [AllRights]/privilege check. FileAttachmentSaveChangesGuard.cs (the #824/#985 SaveChanges-level backstop) does not close this gap: it only validates OTHER entities' FK-SCALAR properties that point AT a FileAttachment principal, never the CONTENT of a FileAttachment entity that is itself being Added. This mutant removes exactly the one statement `pro.SetValue(Entity, null);` inside DoAddPrepareCore's `if (typeof(TModel) != typeof(FileAttachment)) { foreach (var pro in pros) if (pro.PropertyType.GetTypeInfo().IsSubclassOf(typeof(TopBasePoco))) { ... } }` loop (compile-preserving -- the surrounding fkname/fkpro logic is untouched and still compiles with pro.SetValue gone). Checked against FileAttachmentNavPropertyPersistedFieldInvariantTests1024.cs's DoAdd_NestedFileAttachmentNavProperty_AttackerControlledPath_NeverPersisted and its async counterpart, which post a ProductWithOptionalPhoto (a minimal TopBasePoco with an OPTIONAL scalar `FileAttachment? Photo` nav property, declared in FkWriteGateSeventhRoundSqliteTests815.cs, same assembly/namespace) whose Photo is a brand-new FileAttachment with an attacker-chosen Path and a never-before-seen id, PhotoId left null so the separate #815/#824/#828 FK-scalar resolution machinery stays a no-op. Under the mutant, the nested Photo object survives DoAddPrepareCore untouched, DC.Set<TModel>().Add(Entity) cascade-tracks it as Added, and DC.SaveChanges() actually INSERTs it -- the test's own FileAttachments-table lookup for the forged id finds a real row, and Assert.IsNull fails. Positive control (decoupling argument, per .claude/rules/testing.md's 'A mutant's positive control must not touch the mutated decision path'): FkWriteGateSeventhRoundSqliteTests815.DoAdd_OptionalScalarFileId_Unresolvable_PersistsNull_RequestNotRejected also constructs a ProductWithOptionalPhoto and runs it through the SAME DoAdd/DoAddPrepareCore code path, so the mutated loop and its `if (... IsSubclassOf(TopBasePoco))` gate DO execute for this test too -- this is the invariant-result form of decoupling, not a short-circuit. ProductWithOptionalPhoto declares exactly one TopBasePoco-typed property, `Photo`, and that test's Entity never sets Photo at all -- it stays at its CLR default, null. `pro.SetValue(Entity, null)` assigning null to an already-null property is observationally a no-op: whether the statement executes or is deleted, Entity.Photo is null both before and after, DC.Set<TModel>().Add(Entity)'s graph walk finds no FileAttachment reachable via that property either way (there being none to find), and the test's own assertion (an unresolvable PhotoId with no legitimate prior value persists as null, request not rejected) is about the separate FK-scalar gate entirely, never touching Photo's nav-property nulling. The mutated and unmutated forms are therefore provably equal for this specific invocation.
target_symbol: BaseCRUDVM<TModel>.DoAddPrepareCore() -- the `pro.SetValue(Entity, null);` statement inside the TopBasePoco-typed-navigation-property nulling loop, line ~563

red_expected_assertion_patterns.WalkingTec.Mvvm.Core.Test.VM.FileAttachm: #1024 Phase 1 \(precondition \(a\)\): a caller-supplied nested FileAttachment object must never reach the FileAttachments table
#1024 Phase 1 async \(precondition \(a\)\): a caller-supplied nested FileAttachment object must never reach the FileAttachments table via DoAddAsync

red_expected_assertion_patterns_observed: Captured against the committed #1024 Phase 1 fix (stale demo.db under bin/ removed first) with the mutant patch applied: sync test failed with 'Assert.IsNull failed. #1024 Phase 1 (precondition (a)): a caller-supplied nested FileAttachment object must never reach the FileAttachments table — not even under the poster's own tenant, not even with a brand-new id.'; async test failed with 'Assert.IsNull failed. #1024 Phase 1 async (precondition (a)): a caller-supplied nested FileAttachment object must never reach the FileAttachments table via DoAddAsync either'.
